rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The believers are the Prophet’s Companions who affirmed Muhammad; the hypocrites privately tell Jewish leaders Kaʿb b. al-Ashraf and his followers that they share their religion and feign faith only to mock Muhammad and his Companions.
rows.anchor: يعنى صدقوا من أصحاب النبى صلى الله عليه وسلم، { قالوا } لهم: { آمنا } صدقنا بمحمد،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God mocks them in the afterlife by separating them from believers behind a gate-bearing wall on the path, leaving them in darkness and telling them to return for light.
rows.anchor: فقال الله سبحانه: { الله يستهزىء بهم } فى الآخرة إذا ضرب بينهم وبين المؤمنين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God lets the hypocrites persist in their rebellion; they wander back and forth in their error.
rows.anchor: [آية: 15]، يعنى فى ضلالتهم يترددون.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Jews had found Muhammad’s description in the Torah and believed before his mission, expecting an Isaacite prophet; out of envy they rejected the Ishmaelite Muhammad and exchanged faith for denial, making a losing trade without guidance.
rows.anchor: فآمنوا به وظنوا أنه من ولد إسحاق، عليه السلام، فلما بعث محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم من العرب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When God mentioned the spider and fly in the Quran, Jews laughed and called such parables unsuitable; God answers that no modesty prevents Him from giving a parable.
rows.anchor: وذلك أن الله عز وجل ذكر العنكبوت والذباب فى القرآن، فضحكت اليهود، وقالت: ما يشبه هذا من الأمثال،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Believers recognize the parable as truth from God, while the Jewish deniers claim Muhammad invented it himself.
rows.anchor: فيقولون ماذآ أراد الله بهذا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The parable guides believers and misleads many Jews; only the disobedient are led astray by it.
rows.anchor: أى يضل الله بهذا المثل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Jews broke the Torah covenant to worship God alone and believe in Muhammad, rejected Jesus and Muhammad, and accepted some prophets while rejecting others.
rows.anchor: فنقضوا العهد الأول، ونقضوا ما أخذ عليهم فى التوراة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Cutting what God commanded to join means rejecting belief in Muhammad; corruption is acting sinfully, and their loss is punishment, as paralleled in 13:25.
rows.anchor: ونظيرها فى الرعد: { الذين ينقضون عهد الله من بعد ميثاقه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage followed ʿAbd Allah b. Salam’s invitation to nephews Salama and Muhajir: he cited Moses’ prophecy of Ahmad from Ishmael’s descendants and damnation for rejecting him; Salama converted, but Muhajir refused Islam.
rows.anchor: فقال لهما: ألستما تعلمان أن الله عز وجل قال لموسى: إني باعث نبيا من ذرية إسماعيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham’s religion means Islam; rejecting it ruins the People of the Book, while God chose Abraham for prophethood and messengership and counted him among the righteous in the next life.
rows.anchor: يعنى إلا من خسر نفسه من أهل الكتاب،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s command “submit” means be sincere, and Abraham’s “I submit” means sincere to the Lord of the worlds; Abraham charged four sons and Jacob his twelve sons to keep Islam and die as sincere monotheists.
rows.anchor: { إذ قال له ربه أسلم } ، يقول: أخلص، { قال أسلمت } ، يعنى أخلصت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Against the Jews’ claim that Jacob left them Judaism, God says they did not witness his deathbed: Jacob asked whom his sons would worship, and they promised the one God of their forefathers.
rows.anchor: وذلك أن اليهود قالوا للنبى صلى الله عليه وسلم يا محمد، ألست تعلم أن يعقوب يوم مات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham’s and Jacob’s communities have passed and answer for their own deeds; the Jews answer for their own religion and are not questioned about the earlier community.
rows.anchor: يعنى إبراهيم وبنيه، ويعقوب وبنيه، ثم قال لليهود:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jewish leaders Kaʿb b. al-Ashraf and Ibn Suriya concealed the Torah’s account of Muhammad in exchange for small worldly provisions collected annually from ordinary Jews.
rows.anchor: منهم: كعب بن الأشرف، وابن صوريا، كتموا أمر محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم فى التوراة،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who conceal revelation consume fire, receive no divine address or purification of their deeds on Judgment Day, and face painful punishment.
rows.anchor: ولا يكلمهم الله يوم القيامة ولا يزكيهم } ، يقول: ولا يزكى لهم أعمالهم،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They exchanged their prior faith in Muhammad for denial after his mission and chose punishment over forgiveness; their evil acts make them endure the Fire.
rows.anchor: يعني باعوا الهدى الذي كانوا فيه من إيمان بمحمد صلى الله عليه وسلم قبل أن يبعث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Quran was revealed as truth, not in vain; those who dispute it are in distant, prolonged misguidance.
rows.anchor: يعني لفي ضلال بعيد، يعني طويل.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The companions of the chamber asked God to pour patience over them and keep their feet steady in battle; “pour” also describes pouring molten metal in 18:96.
rows.anchor: يعنى ألق، أصبب علينا صبرا، كقوله سبحانه:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: David alone faced Goliath, despite appearing unarmed; three stones joined into one, a gust removed Goliath’s helmet, and David’s stone struck through his brain, routing the unbelievers and killing thirty thousand.
rows.anchor: وألقت الريح البيضة عن رأسه، فرماه فوقع الحجر فى دماغه حتى خرج من أسفله،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Afterward David asked Saul for half his wealth and kingdom; Saul envied and expelled him, later regretted it, and Israel loved David more than Saul.
rows.anchor: وطلب داود نصف مال طالوت ونصف ملكه، فحسده طالوت على صنيعه وأخرجه،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A deferred debt’s amount and due date should be written; a fair scribe writes between buyer and seller without increasing the debtor’s amount or reducing the creditor’s right; scribes were few in Muhammad’s time.
rows.anchor: يعنى اكتبوا الدين والأجل، { وليكتب } الكاتب بين البائع والمشترى،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The debtor must dictate the record, fear God, and omit none of what is owed; the warning against shortchanging also appears in 7:85.
rows.anchor: يعنى المطلوب، ثم خوف المطلوب، فقال عز وجل: { وليتق الله ربه ولا يبخس منه شيئا }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If the debtor is ignorant, mentally impaired, weak, unable to dictate, or cannot speak, the creditor’s guardian dictates fairly, neither adding nor subtracting.
rows.anchor: يعنى أو عاجزا، أو به حمق،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The right-holder’s representative dictates for an incapable debtor and must be fair, matching the same no-increase, no-decrease standard imposed on the debtor.
rows.anchor: { فليملل وليه } ، يعنى ولى الحق، فليملل هو { بالعدل } ، يعنى بالحق،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For a debt, use two acceptable male witnesses or one man and two women; if one woman forgets, the other reminds her, and a summoned witness should serve when free.
rows.anchor: يقول: ولا يشهد الرجل على حقه إلا مرضيا إن كان الشاهد رجلا أو امرأة.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Do not tire of recording even a small amount through its due date: writing better records the term and protects property, is just, reliable for testimony, and less likely to create doubt.
rows.anchor: ولا تملوا، وكل شىء فى القرآن تسأموا، يعنى تملوا،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here “more likely” means more suitable: written evidence is more likely to bring testimony in 5:108 and to comfort the wives in 33:51.
rows.anchor: ذلك أدنى أن يأتوا بالشهادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An immediate cash trade with no term may go unwritten; sales should be witnessed, but a scribe or witness should not be pressured when occupied if another can be found.
rows.anchor: ليس فيها أجل، { فليس عليكم جناح } ، يعنى حرج،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wronging a scribe or witness is sinful; God commands the parties to fear Him and knows all their deeds.
rows.anchor: وإن تضاروا الكاتب والشاهد وما نهيتم عنه، فإنه إثم بكم،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When traveling without a scribe or writing materials, the debtor should provide the creditor with a held pledge; if trusted without collateral, he must repay the debt entrusted to him and fear God.
rows.anchor: فليرتهن الذى عليه الحق من المطلوب،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Witnesses must testify accurately before the judge and not conceal testimony; whoever hides it sins in his heart, and God knows whether testimony is given or suppressed.
rows.anchor: فلا تكتموا الشهادة، قال: { ومن يكتمها } ولا يشهد بها عند الحاكم،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Believers must obey God’s commands and obligations, stand firm alongside the Prophet in campaigns, guard against the enemy until it abandons its religion for theirs, and avoid disobedience to attain success.
rows.anchor: على أمر الله عز وجل وفرائضه، { وصابروا } مع النبى صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: A report attributed to Ibn ʿAbbas quotes the Prophet’s pact with Najran: tribute in garments, protection for people, property, and Christian institutions, and provisions on loans, taxes, and justice.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس، رضى الله عنه، قال: كتب رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم لأهل نجران:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pact lists Abu Sufyan b. Harb, Ghaylan b. ʿAmr, Malik b. ʿAwf, al-Aqraʿ b. Habis, and al-Mughira as witnesses; the account says Abu Bakr copied a document from the Prophet’s original.
rows.anchor: شهد أبو سفيان بن حرب، وغيلان بن عمرو، ومالك بن عوف النضرى، والأقرع ابن حابس،

rows.speaker: سالم بن أبي الجعد
rows.claim: In a report about Najran, ʿAli refused to criticize ʿUmar, telling the delegation that ʿUmar had acted wisely.
rows.anchor: عن سالم بن أبى الجعد، قال: لو كان عليا طاعنا على عمر بن الخطاب،

rows.speaker: سالم بن أبي الجعد
rows.claim: Salem’s account says Najran’s population grew to forty thousand fighters, conflict arose, and ʿUmar refused a request to return after their reconciliation, sending groups to Syria, Iraq, and elsewhere.
rows.anchor: قال: كثروا حتى صاروا أربعين ألف مقاتل، فخاف المسلمون أن يميلوا عليهم،

rows.speaker: الهذيل
rows.claim: Hudhayl reports that 3:186 has its words fronted, while noting that he did not hear this from Muqatil.
rows.anchor: [آل عمران: 186]، فيها تقديم، ولم أسمع مقاتل.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Guardians should test orphans’ understanding until puberty and return their assets when they show religious uprightness and sound financial judgment; they must not consume assets wastefully or hasten to take them before maturity.
rows.anchor: { وابتلوا اليتامى } ، يقول: اختبروا عقولهم، { حتى إذا بلغوا النكاح } ، يعنى الحلم،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A wealthy guardian must abstain; a poor one may borrow reasonably and repay if able. Witness the transfer at maturity; God is the best witness. The verse concerns Thabit b. Rifaʿa, whose uncle held his inheritance.
rows.anchor: نزلت فى ثابت ابن رفاعة وعمه، وذلك أن رفاعة توفى وترك ابنه ثابت،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Quraysh disbelievers will suddenly face the Resurrection and lament neglecting God’s remembrance; their evil deeds appear as an ugly, foul-smelling figure that demands they carry it, then rides their backs.
rows.anchor: أتاه عمله الخبيث فى صورة حبشى، أشوه، منتن الريح، كريه المنظر،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: At the end of the month Abraham sees Venus from a cave; its setting, then the setting of the larger, brighter moon and sun, proves that none is his enduring Lord, and he seeks guidance lest he stray.
rows.anchor: دنا من باب السرب، وذلك فى آخر الشهر، فرأى الزهرة أول الليل من خلال السرب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After recognizing the enduring Creator, Abraham leaves the cave, rejects his people’s idols, and declares devoted worship of the Creator of the heavens and earth alone.
rows.anchor: قال لهم: ما تعبدون؟ قالوا: نعبد ما ترى،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When Nimrod claimed to give life and death by killing one man and sparing another, Abraham challenged him to bring the sun from the west; Nimrod was confounded.
rows.anchor: فعمد نمروذ إلى إنسان فقتله، وجاء بآخر فتركه،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham’s people feared their powerless idols would ruin or afflict him; he says they neither hear, see, benefit nor harm, and only fears God’s will, whose knowledge encompasses all.
rows.anchor: وهى لا تسمع ولا تبصر شيئا، ولا تنفع ولا تضر، وتنحتونها بأيديكم،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham asks whether monotheists or idolaters deserve security: the latter associate many gods without scriptural authority, even equating great and small, male and female deities.
rows.anchor: يعنى كتابا فيه حجتكم بأن معه شريكا،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The faithful who do not mix belief with shirk are secure and guided; Abraham’s people conceded his argument, and God granted him this proof and raises whom He wills.
rows.anchor: يعنى ولم خلطوا تصديقهم بشرك، فلم يعبدوا غيره،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God guided Noah before Abraham, then lists prophets among Noah’s descendants—including David, Solomon, Job, Joseph, Moses, Aaron, Jesus, and others—whom He favored with prophethood above the worlds.
rows.anchor: يعنى من ذرية نوح، { داوود وسليمان وأيوب ويوسف وموسى وهارون وكذلك }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prohibitions include shirk, honoring parents, killing daughters from fear of poverty, public or secret adultery, and killing protected life except by retaliation, stoning of a married adulterer, or apostasy; pre-Islamic camel taboos are not forbidden here.
rows.anchor: يعني دفن البنات وهن أحياء، { من إملاق } ، يعني خشية الفقر،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Foul deeds” means adultery, public or secret; lawful execution is limited to retaliation, a married adulterer, or an apostate from Islam.
rows.anchor: يعني بالقصاص والثيب الزاني بالرجم، والمرتد عن الإسلام،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Orphan property may be used only to grow it through profit until the orphan reaches eighteen; fulfill measures and weights fairly and within each person’s capacity.
rows.anchor: إلا ليثمر لليتيم ماله بالأرباح، { حتى يبلغ أشده } ، يعني ثماني عشرة سنة،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Speak justly even about relatives and fulfill God’s covenant with people; these commands and prohibitions are meant to prompt remembrance.
rows.anchor: يعنى أولى قربى إذا تكلمتم فقولوا الحق، وإن كان ذو قرابتك فقل فيه الحق،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The straight path is the upright religion; avoid paths of forbidden error that divide people from God’s way. These ordinances are clear and binding on all Adam’s descendants, never abrogated.
rows.anchor: فهذه الآيات المحكمات لم ينسخهن شىء من جميع الكتب،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Torah completed God’s promised favor to the Israelites who did good, as foretold in 28:5–6; it details all things, guides from error, and offers mercy so they believe in resurrection and judgment.
rows.anchor: إلى آيتين [القصص: 5، 6]. ثم قال: { وتفصيلا لكل شيء } والتوراة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh threatens to cut off opposite limbs, the right hand and left foot or left hand and right foot, then crucify all the magicians.
rows.anchor: يعنى اليد اليمنى والرجل اليسرى، أو الرجل اليمنى واليد اليسرى،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The magicians accept that they return to God and say Pharaoh resents only their belief in the signs of the hand and staff; they ask patience through mutilation and crucifixion, remaining sincere Muslims.
rows.anchor: يعنى صدقنا باليد والعصا آيتان من ربنا،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh crucified the magicians that same day; they were unbelieving sorcerers at dawn and Muslim martyrs by evening after believing Moses.
rows.anchor: فصلبهم فرعون من يومه، فكانوا أول النهار سحرة كفارا، وآخر النهار شهداء مسلمين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh’s nobles fear Moses and Israel will kill Egypt’s sons and spare its women, abandoning Pharaoh’s worship; Pharaoh orders the boys killed and women spared, but God stops this by drowning him.
rows.anchor: يعنى الأشراف { من قوم فرعون أتذر موسى وقومه } ،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses tells Israel to seek God’s help and endure: Egypt belongs to God, who grants it to whomever He wills, and Paradise is for monotheist God-fearers; after earlier infanticide they now suffer impossible labor, but God may destroy Pharaoh and install them as successors.
rows.anchor: فى التقديم: { استعينوا بالله } على فرعون وقومه،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses’ prediction that God would destroy Pharaoh and make Israel successors in Egypt fulfills the promise in 28:5–6; afterward they adopted the calf.
rows.anchor: ففعل الله ذلك بهم، فأهلك عدوهم واستخلفهم فى الأرض، فاتخذوا العجل.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If a Meccan polytheist seeks protection after fifty days, the Prophet must secure him from killing, let him hear the Quran, and return him safely if he refuses it; should he later fight and be captured, he may be killed.
rows.anchor: فإن استأمنك أحد من المشركين بعد خمسين يوما فأمنه من القتل،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Hudaybiyya allies Khuzaʿa, Banu Mudlij, and Banu Khuzayma retain their four-month pact if they keep it; Muslims must honor it through its end, counted from the sacrifice day.
rows.anchor: ثم استثنى خزاعة، وبنى مدلج، وبنى خزيمة، الذين أجلهم أربعة أشهر،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Quraysh broke their truce; if they gain power they will respect neither kinship nor treaty, though their tongues please Muslims while their hearts conceal hostility.
rows.anchor: يقول: لا يحفظوا فيكم قرابة ولا عهدا،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abu Sufyan gave camels, food, and other goods to turn people from following Muhammad, trading belief for little worldly gain; the Meccans thereby oppose Islam and violate kinship and covenant.
rows.anchor: وذلك أن أبا سفيان كان يعطي الناقة والطعام والشىء ليصد بذلك الناس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rain and crops, hearing and sight, life from semen and death from the living, and governance belong to God; Quraysh acknowledge this, so they should abandon shirk and fear punishment.
rows.anchor: من { والأرض } ، يعنى النبات والثمار،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is the true Lord; after truth only falsehood remains, and His prior decree means rebellious people will not believe.
rows.anchor: فماذا بعد عبادة الحق والإيمان إلا الباطل، { فأنى تصرفون }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: No alleged partner can originate creation from a drop without model or consultation, then revive it; Quraysh concede God does both, so their denial of His unity is incoherent.
rows.anchor: يقول: فمن أين تكذبون بتوحيد الله إذا زعمتم أن مع الله إلها آخر.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wrongdoers obstruct Islam, seek to distort it, and deny resurrection; they cannot escape God or find relatives to protect them, and their punishment is doubled because they would not hear or see Quranic faith.
rows.anchor: يعني دين الإسلام، { ويبغونها عوجا } ، يقول: ويريدون بملة الإسلام زيفا،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They have cheated themselves of salvation, and the objects they fabricated as gods have disappeared.
rows.anchor: يعنى بسابقى الله { في الأرض } هربا حتى يجزيهم بأعمالهم الخبيثة،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “La jarama” means certainly: these unbelievers are the greatest losers in the afterlife.
rows.anchor: { لا جرم } حقا، { أنهم في الآخرة هم الأخسرون }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph’s brothers come to Jacob at the evening prayer, claiming they went hunting and left Joseph guarding their belongings; the wolf ate him, they say, and Jacob will not believe them even if truthful.
rows.anchor: { وجآءوا أباهم } يعقوب { عشآء يبكون } [آية: 16] صلاة العتمة.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After throwing Joseph into the well, the brothers stripped his shirt and put a slaughtered lamb’s blood on it; seeing it intact, Jacob suspects them and wryly says the wolf spared the garment.
rows.anchor: وذلك أنهم حين ألقوه في البئر انتزعوا ثيابه، وهو قميصه،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jacob says his patience will be beautiful, without despair, and seeks God’s help against their account; he cried and could not sleep or eat, which Muqatil says explains Jewish wailing when reading Torah.
rows.anchor: يعنى صبرى صبرا حسنا لا جزع فيه،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God granted people unasked gifts out of mercy among the blessings already mentioned; people wrong themselves through sins and are ungrateful for blessings because they do not worship Him.
rows.anchor: ما لم تسألوه ولا طلبتموه، ولكن أعطيتكم من رحمتي،

rows.speaker: أبو صالح
rows.claim: Abu Salih says the reading with min means God gave things they did not ask for; a reading without min means He answered their requests.
rows.anchor: سمعت أبا صالح في قوله عز وجل: { من كل ما سألتموه } ، قال: أعطاكم ما لم تسألوه،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On a winter Friday night in the Holy Land, lost Moses saw fire, told his wife and child to wait, and hoped to bring a flame for warmth or find a guide; it was the Lord’s light, and angelic praise frightened him before God gave him calm.
rows.anchor: ليلة الجمعة في الشتاء بأرض المقدسة، { فقال لأهله } يعني امرأته وولده { امكثوا } مكانكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: At the valley Tuwa, God calls Moses and orders him to remove sandals made from the skin of an unritually dead donkey; Tuwa is the valley’s name and means the purified valley.
rows.anchor: جلد حمار ميت غير ذكى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God created the seven heavens, seven earths, and their inhabitants for a real purpose, not in play or without cause.
rows.anchor: يعنى السموات السبع والأرضين السبع { وما بينهما } من الخلق { لاعبين }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Against Najran Christians’ claim that Jesus is God’s son, God says a child, if intended, would be taken from the angels; He does not beget one, and truth smashes their falsehood.
rows.anchor: وذلك أن نصارى نجران السيد والعاقب، ومن معهما، قالوا: عيسى ابن الله،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ayka means a tree thicket where doom and wild date trees were common; its people denied Shuaib, who was Abrahamic-Midianite but not their own descendant, explaining why this passage omits “their brother.”
rows.anchor: يعنى غيطة الشجر، كان أكثر الشجرة الدوم، وهو المقل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Shuaib asks whether they fear God, declares himself a trustworthy messenger, urges obedience, and says he asks no payment for belief: his reward rests only with the Lord of the worlds.
rows.anchor: ولم يكن شعيب من نسبهم، فلذلك لم يقل عز وجل أخوهم شعيب،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Shuaib orders full measure and a straight scale—qistas is the Roman word for balance—and forbids cheating people of rights or spreading corruption through sins.
rows.anchor: يعنى بالميزان المستقيم، والميزان بلغة الروم القسطاس،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He warns them to fear the Creator of earlier peoples, including Noah’s, Salih’s, and Lot’s communities, which were punished; they reject Shuaib as bewitched, merely human, and a liar.
rows.anchor: { واتقوا } يقول: واخشوا أن يعذبكم فى الدنيا { الذي خلقكم و } خلق { والجبلة } يعنى الخليقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After ten years, Moses traveled with his family on Friday night, saw a light by Mount Sinai, and sought directions or a burning branch to warm them because he had lost his way.
rows.anchor: { فلما قضى موسى الأجل } السنين العشر، { وسار بأهله } ليلة الجمعة { آنس } يعني رأى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses left his wife, child, and flock in the wilderness between Egypt and Midian; she remained there thirty years until a shepherd found her and took her to her father.
rows.anchor: فترك موسى، عليه السلام، امرأته وولده في البرية بين مصر ومدين، ثم استقام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This verse addresses weak Muslims in Mecca unable to profess openly: God’s earth is wide, meaning Medina, where they can openly worship Him alone.
rows.anchor: نزلت فى ضعفاء مسلمى أهل مكة إن كنتم فى ضيق بمكة من إظهار الإيمان،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God reminds migrants that everyone dies and returns for judgment; faithful, righteous migrants receive eternal rooms with rivers, and those patient through migration trust God despite lacking money or livelihood in Medina.
rows.anchor: ثم خوفهم الموت ليهاجروا، فقال تعالى: { كل نفس ذآئقة الموت ثم إلينا ترجعون } [آية: 57]

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: To ease migrants’ fear of lacking provisions, God points to animals and birds that carry no food yet are fed wherever they go; He also provides for emigrants and hears their concerns.
rows.anchor: { من دآبة } فى الأرض أو طير { لا تحمل } يعنى لا ترفع { رزقها } معها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Meccan polytheists admit God alone created heaven and earth and subjected sun and moon, so why deny His oneness? God expands or constricts provision as He wills and knows all.
rows.anchor: { من خلق السماوات والأرض وسخر الشمس والقمر ليقولن الله } وحده خلقهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God gives every kind of parable in the Quran, but Meccans call a demanded sign false, as they dismissed the splitting of the moon as magic.
rows.anchor: كما كذبوا فى انشقاق القمر حين قالوا: هذا سحر.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God seals with unbelief the hearts of those ignorant of His oneness; when warned of worldly punishment they deny it.
rows.anchor: يقول: هكذا يختم الله عز وجل بالكفر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After al-Nadr b. al-Harith demanded immediate punishment, God tells Muhammad not to be provoked by the unconvinced; Badr killed al-Nadr, ʿAli beheaded him, and the dead are displayed to the Fire morning and evening.
rows.anchor: هذا قول النضر بن الحارث القرشى من بنى عبدالدار بن قصى، فأنزل الله تعالى:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Luqman received wisdom as knowledge and understanding, not prophethood; gratitude for God’s gifts benefits the grateful through good works, while God needs no worship and remains praised in His dominion.
rows.anchor: أعطيناه العلم والفهم من غير نبوة فهذه نعمة،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Luqman’s son was named Anʿum; he counseled him against shirk, the gravest injustice, and his son and wife eventually became Muslim through persistence.
rows.anchor: وإذ قال لقمان لابنه } واسم ابنه أنعم { وهو يعظه } يعنى عز وجل يؤدبه

rows.speaker: قتادة بن دعامة
rows.claim: Qatada reports that Luqman was flat-nosed and from Abyssinia.
rows.anchor: عن قتادة بن دعامة، قال: كان لقمان رجلا أفطس من أرض الحبشة،

rows.speaker: الهذيل
rows.claim: Hudhayl says he did not hear Muqatil report the preceding description.
rows.anchor: قال هذيل: ولم أسمع مقاتلا.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The parents in this passage are Saʿd b. Abi Waqqas’s father Malik and mother Hamna bint Sufyan; she bore him weakness upon weakness and weaned him over two years; thanks to God means gratitude for guidance to Islam.
rows.anchor: سعد بن أبي وقاص بوالديه، يعنى أباه اسمه مالك، وأمه حمنة بنت سفيان بن أمية بن عبد شمس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Saʿd must not obey parents who urge shirk, yet should treat them kindly; he should follow the Prophet’s religion and remember that all return to God for judgment.
rows.anchor: فلا تطعهما } في الشرك { وصاحبهما في الدنيا معروفا } يعنى بإحسان،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Luqman’s son Anʿum asks how God could know a sin committed where no one sees him.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن لقمان أنعم لأبيه: يا أبت، إن عملت بالخطيئة حيث لا يرانى أحد كيف يعلمه الله،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Even a mustard seed’s weight hidden in a hollow green rock beneath the earth, in heaven, or anywhere on earth is brought by God; He subtly retrieves it and knows its location.
rows.anchor: وهي خضراء مجوفة لها ثلاث شعب على لون السماء،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Luqman commands prayer, enjoining monotheism and forbidding evil, and patience through injury in this work; enduring it is among the firm obligations God imposed.
rows.anchor: يعني التوحيد { وانه عن المنكر } يعني الشر الذي لا يعرف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Do not turn arrogantly away from poor people or walk boastfully; God dislikes the proud person who fails to thank Him for blessings.
rows.anchor: لا تعرض وجهك عن فقراء الناس إذا كلموك فخرا بالخيلاء والعظمة،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The trust is obedience carrying reward and punishment: the heavens, earth, and mountains refused from fear of punishment, while Adam accepted after learning its terms and soon sinned; the human is Adam, unjust to himself and ignorant of the consequence.
rows.anchor: { إنا عرضنا الأمانة } وهى الطاعة { على السماوات والأرض والجبال } على الثواب والعقاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The trust was offered so hypocrites and polytheists would be punished for betraying it, rejecting messengers, and breaking the primordial covenant made when descendants were brought from Adam.
rows.anchor: فنقضوا هذه المعرفة وتركوا الطاعة يعنى التوحيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Believers and believing women receive God’s pardon and mercy because they honored the trust and kept that covenant.
rows.anchor: بما وفوا بالأمانة ولم ينقضوا الميثاق { وكان الله غفورا } لذنوبهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The person exemplified is Abu Hudhayfa b. al-Mughira: hardship makes him repentantly call to God, but after relief he forgets that prayer and sets up rivals to lead him away from Islam.
rows.anchor: يعنى أبا حذيفة بن المغيرة بن عبدالله المخزومى { ضر } يعنى بلاء أو شدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The obedient night worshipper is ʿAmmar b. Yasir, who fears punishment and hopes for Paradise; unlike Abu Hudhayfa, he knows the promised afterlife recompense, exemplifying people of understanding.
rows.anchor: وهو عمار بن ياسر { آنآء الليل ساجدا } يعنى ساعات الليل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Believers should fear God; good-doers receive Paradise, and God’s wide earth means Medina. Those patient in emigration receive Paradise and provisions without measure.
rows.anchor: { وأرض الله واسعة } يعنى المدينة { إنما يوفى الصابرون أجرهم } يعنى جزاءهم الجنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Angels tell believers they were their protectors in worldly life and remain so in the afterlife; in Paradise they receive whatever they desire and request, a welcome gift from the Forgiving, Merciful God.
rows.anchor: ما تشتهي أنفسكم ولكم فيها ما تدعون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The best speaker is Muhammad: he calls people to monotheism, does good, and declares himself sincerely Muslim.
rows.anchor: يعنى التوحيد، { وعمل صالحا وقال إنني من المسلمين }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because Abu Jahl harmed Muhammad, whom the Prophet disliked, God commanded forgiveness and forbearance; patience in restraining anger may turn an enemy into a close ally, and Muhammad must seek refuge from Satan.
rows.anchor: وذلك أن أبا جهل كان يؤذي النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم، وكان النبي مبغضا له، يكره رؤيته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “The sky with woven tracks” resembles rippled patterns formed by wind over sand.
rows.anchor: يعني مثل الطرائق التي تكون في الرمل من الريح، ومثل تصيبه الريح،

rows.speaker: أبو صالح
rows.claim: Abu Salih offers another explanation for the sky’s tracks: its beautiful creation.
rows.anchor: قال أبو صالح: { والسمآء ذات الحبك } الخلق الحسن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Meccans differ about the Quran, with some believing and some rejecting it; the false conjecturers are turned away from Quranic faith.
rows.anchor: { إنكم } يا أهل مكة { لفي قول } يعني القرآن { مختلف } [آية: 8] شك يؤمن به بعضكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The cursed conjecturers are seventeen liars whom al-Walid b. al-Mughira sent in groups of four to festival roads to call Muhammad sorcerer, madman, poet, soothsayer, and liar; distracted, they mockingly ask when Judgment comes.
rows.anchor: وكانوا سبعة عشر رجلا، فقال لهم الوليد بن المغيرة المخزومي: لينطلق كل أربعة منكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People must flee to God from sins, worship no other deity, and heed the clear warning of punishment; Meccans call Muhammad a magician or madman, like earlier transgressive peoples who accused their messengers.
rows.anchor: فردوا عليه إنك ساحر مجنون، يقول الله تعالى { كذلك } يعنى هكذا { مآ أتى الذين من قبلهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sun and moon have 180 risings and 180 settings, allowing people to count years and calculate time.
rows.anchor: مطالعهما ومغاربهما ثمانين ومائة مطلع، وثمانين ومائة مغرب، لتعلموا بها عدد السنين والحساب.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Low plants without stems and trees with stems prostrate through their shadows as the sun moves; the sky is raised 500 years above earth, and the balance establishes justice, requiring people not to cheat in measures.
rows.anchor: { والنجم } يعني كل نبت ليس له ساق { والشجر } كل نبت له ساق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Weigh with justice” means use the balance’s tongue fairly and do not reduce weights; earth is made for creatures, and palm fruits emerge from their coverings like 41:47, including wheat and barley.
rows.anchor: يعني اللسان بالعدل { ولا تخسروا } يعني ولا تنقصوا
